extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (patent attorneys/agents) who receive client referrals from non-practitioner third parties
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and enforceable professional-conduct standards for USPTO-registered practitioners who provide patent legal services to inventors referred by non-practitioner third parties (e.g., invention promotion/marketing companies). Covers conflicts, informed consent, communication, fee-sharing, independence of judgment, delegation, and related duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain informed consent for limited-scope representation (37 C.F.R. § 11.102(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must obtain the client's informed consent when limiting the scope of representation (e.g., preparing and filing an application but not prosecuting it). The respondent admitted failing to obtain such consent where representation was limited only to filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain meaningful informed consent before accepting a limited-scope engagement; disclose that representation is only for specific tasks and not ongoing prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate scope of representation and basis of fee (37 C.F.R. § 11.105(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must advise clients at the outset of the representation about the scope of representation and the basis or rate of the fee. Respondent failed to advise inventor-applicants of scope and basis of fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At intake clearly state what services will and will not be provided, the fee structure, and client responsibilities; document the communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act with reasonable diligence and promptness (37 C.F.R. § 11.103)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must act with reasonable diligence and promptness, including promptly advising clients of Office Actions and Notices of Abandonment. Respondent failed to notify clients of Office Actions and allowed many applications to become abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor filings and Office communications; promptly notify clients of Office correspondence and take timely action or obtain client instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain matters sufficiently to permit informed decisions (37 C.F.R. § 11.104(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must explain material risks and reasonably available alternatives so clients can make informed decisions. Respondent failed to explain risks of third-party payor arrangements and benefits/risks of chosen patent protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear explanations (e.g., differences between provisional/design/utility, expiration consequences, third-party payment risks) and confirm client understanding and consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain informed consent when responsibilities are materially limited by conflicts (37 C.F.R. § 11.107(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a practitioner's responsibilities are materially limited (e.g., by contract with a referrer or by personal financial interest), the practitioner must obtain the client's informed consent. Respondent represented clients where representation was materially limited without consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify potential material limitations/conflicts before agreeing to represent and obtain explicit informed consent after full disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain informed consent before accepting compensation from a third party (37 C.F.R. § 11.108(f)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepting compensation for representing a client from someone other than the client requires the client's informed consent. Respondent accepted compensation from WPM without obtaining such consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose who will pay, the terms, and material risks/alternatives; obtain documented informed consent that is more than mere authorization of third-party payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid interference with independent professional judgment and third-party direction (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.108(f)(2) & 11.504(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must not allow a third party who pays for services to direct or regulate the practitioner's professional judgment. Respondent allowed WPM personnel to direct which types of applications to file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independently evaluate client objectives and determine appropriate patent strategy; do not follow non-practitioner directives about legal decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abide by client's decisions and reasonably consult about means (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.102(a) & 11.104(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must abide by clients' decisions concerning objectives and reasonably consult with them about how to accomplish those objectives. Respondent failed to consult with clients about means and objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage clients in selection of strategy; document consultations about methods, priorities, and prosecution plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promptly inform client of decisions/circumstances requiring consent and keep client reasonably informed (37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(1),(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must promptly inform clients of matters requiring consent and keep them reasonably informed of status. Respondent did not promptly inform clients that provisional applications would expire or of abandonments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notify clients of deadlines (e.g., provisional expiration), Office Actions, and abandonment; ensure clients understand consequences of inaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not share legal fees with non-practitioners (37 C.F.R. § 11.504(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must not share legal fees with non-practitioner third parties. Respondent allowed WPM to bill clients for legal services in a way that resulted in impermissible fee-sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify amounts charged to inventors and ensure the practitioner receives the full legal fee or that any retained amounts are properly returned to the inventor; question referrers about fee remittance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not partner with or assist non-practitioners in the practice of law (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.504(b) & 11.505)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner may not form a partnership with a non-practitioner if the partnership's activities include practice of law, nor assist a non-practitioner to practice law in violation of legal-profession rules. Respondent assisted WPM's non-practitioner employees in consulting/giving advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid arrangements that create de facto partnerships; obtain and review documents exchanged between referrer and inventor to assess whether the referrer is engaging in practice before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise independent professional judgment and render candid advice (37 C.F.R. § 11.201)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must exercise independent judgment and provide candid advice, including independently assessing the suitability of the sought patent protection rather than 'filling a purchase order.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform your own assessment (e.g., appropriateness of provisional vs utility vs design) and communicate your evaluation to the client regardless of what the referrer advised or sold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain copies of documents exchanged between referrer and inventor to assess referrer's role
rubrics_metrics.description: When receiving referrals from a non-practitioner, the practitioner is reasonably expected to obtain copies of all documents exchanged between the company and the inventor to understand whether the company is engaging in practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request and review advertising, search/marketing reports, engagement forms, signed oaths/certifications, and other communications to determine whether the referrer is conducting legal work or directing inventors improperly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question amounts charged by the referrer to ensure no impermissible fee-sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner is reasonably expected to question carefully the inventor and referring non-practitioner about amounts charged so the practitioner knows whether the entire amount for legal services is being remitted to the practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify fee flow; if undistributed compensation is retained by the referrer and not returned to the inventor, a fee-sharing violation likely exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure inventor review and valid signatures before filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must ensure inventor-applicants have reviewed finalized applications before filing and that signatures (oaths, powers of attorney, micro-entity certifications) are properly obtained. Respondent filed applications without ensuring inventor review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm inventor review of the final application and validate that inventor signatures were made knowingly and after review; do not rely solely on referrer-obtained signatures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enter into written representation agreements and disclose limited scope when applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner should have written representation agreements and should inform clients when representation is limited in scope. Respondent had not entered into written agreements or informed clients of limited scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use written engagement letters that state scope, fees, who will pay, communication expectations, and retention/termination terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not delegate core client-communication responsibilities to third parties or subordinates
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner may not delegate their ethical responsibilities to communicate with clients regarding the substance of representation to subordinates or third parties. Respondent generally did not communicate with clients and relied on WPM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directly communicate substantive legal advice, material risks, and status to clients; use delegates only for administrative tasks and supervise them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible reliance on liaison/agent only with client consent
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner may communicate with a corporate liaison or foreign agent who conveys instructions only where there is a bona fide liaison and the practitioner is aware the client consented to having instructions conveyed through that person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain and document client consent before relying on an intermediary for instructions; ensure the liaison's role is bona fide and transparent to the client.
